correctness.rationale: The periodic generator has stationary orientation densities proportional to reciprocal speed. An explicit bounded periodic corrector has constant interorientation difference L/J and satisfies the two Poisson equations. Its jump quadratic variation yields D=L^2/(2 I J) for every starting state. With mean constraints, minimizing reversal cost is a strict linear optimization for unequal speeds; the speed ratio is controlled by the sign of a quadratic with one root greater than 1, giving uniqueness and sharp 32/27. Its f-down-to-zero expansion is verified and implies no fraction-uniform ceiling. A separate upwind Markov-chain corrector diagnostic at three mesh sizes for three choices, 240 numerical envelope checks, and exact symbolic identities agree. The finite cases are diagnostics, not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim is restricted to the sharp simultaneous speed-and-reversal allocation under fixed spatial arithmetic means, including uniqueness, equal-half factor 32/27, the singular 1/(4f) enhancement and exact contrast boundary. General velocity-jump diffusion and homogenization methods are attributed to earlier work. In actual research-index queries and inspected accessible primary source material no statement was found that imposes both budgets and determines the global optimizer or narrow-patch unboundedness. The close Lutscher–Hillen periodic homogenization is acknowledged as implying much of the nonoptimized effective diffusivity. Angelani–Garra 2019 remains inaccessible in full and a genuine priority risk; abstract noncoverage is not asserted.
residual_risks: The complete 2019 Angelani–Garra source remains inaccessible and could contain an equivalent optimized profile.
The 2021 general homogenization result supplies an overlapping mathematical starting point; the novelty is the budget envelope, not generic diffusivity.
Different authors normalize tumbling as orientation randomization rather than certain reversal, changing numerical rate factors but not the gain ratio.
Other uncatalogued prior work may derive the same constrained extremum.

value.rationale: The joint budget constraint naturally models motility landscapes whose total local speed and reversal activity are limited independently. The exact optimum demonstrates a finite sharp gain 32/27 in equal patches, supplies the design boundary for strict enhancement and proves a mathematically surprising lack of any global enhancement ceiling without local-amplitude constraints. The narrow-patch singularity shows why mean-only engineering budgets are insufficient. The mathematical object, invariant and claimed sharpness are motivated before computation; the theorem is not merely re-evaluating a known table.
